tools.description: AI-first code editor (VS Code fork) with natural language code generation and Tab completion. Cursor 2.0 supports 8 parallel AI agents on same task. Valued at $9.9B with full VS Code extension compatibility.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-08-18] description flagged: Fetched cursor.com and /pricing: free Hobby tier, Pro $20/mo. SpaceX's $60B acquisition of Anysphere closed 2026-08-14 (CNBC, site itself) — the '$9.9B valuation' claim is now wrong.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.description: AI pair programmer providing real-time code suggestions in VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse, and Xcode. Agent mode for multi-file changes with test validation; contributes 46% of code for active users. Accelerates coding by 55%.

tools.name: Google Antigravity
tools.description: Agent-first development platform from Google that lets AI agents take actions across an IDE, terminal and browser. Hosts Science Skills for connecting research workflows to 30+ life-science databases. Launched alongside Gemini for Science (May 2026).

tools.name: Grantable
tools.description: Chat-first AI 'coworker' that remembers your organisation, past proposals and funder context. Built-in prospecting via GrantGraph (11M+ data points from 990 filings, public records and web research) covering 130,000+ funders. Pricing from $24/month.

tools.name: GrantBoost
tools.description: Template-based AI grant writing for nonprofit and research grants. Pick a grant type, fill in organisational details and the AI drafts proposal sections. Works best for common, well-known grant categories. Pricing from $19.99/month.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-08-18] grantboost.com is a parked GoDaddy for-sale domain; live product at grantboost.io. Plans $32/$49/$66/mo (no free tier seen; '$19.99' stale). Academic fit: site explicitly lists universities/research institutions seeking federal grants.

tools.name: Granted AI
tools.description: Full-lifecycle grant platform: discovery across 85,000+ grants from 144 sources, funder research over 133,000+ foundations, AI-coached drafting from uploaded RFPs, simulated committee review and compliance checks. Free tier available; paid plans from $29/month.

tools.name: Instrumentl
tools.description: Grant discovery, tracking and lightweight proposal support with a database of 400,000+ active funding opportunities. Strong for academic researchers and larger nonprofits managing complex grant portfolios. Plans from ~$179/month (billed annually).

tools.name: Research Kick
tools.description: AI research ideation tool identifying research gaps across 1B+ papers from Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, Scite, and PubMed. GPT-4o with proprietary reasoning to prevent hallucinations. Used by 2,000+ academics.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-08-18] description flagged: Both catalog URLs redirect to chatacademia.com; founder (Mushtaq Bilal) confirmed rebrand of Research Kick Chat to ChatAcademia. Description stale: old name, GPT-4o claim. Now $15-45/mo plans, free trial, 8+ databases, grant search.

tools.name: Amberscript
tools.description: Cloud transcription for research interviews: machine drafts in minutes (90+ languages, ~85% accuracy) or human-verified transcripts (>99%, 18+ languages) with NDA-bound transcribers. Data stored only in Western Europe; GDPR, ISO 27001/9001. Word/TXT export, speech-to-text API.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: EU-hosted transcription with an optional professional human-correction tier for verbatim accuracy — the step between DIY Whisper and a transcription bureau Adoption: University of Barcelona case study on sensitive-interview transcription (vendor-published, so partly marketing); cited in a fetched arXiv paper's methods as 'GDPR-compliant software Amberscript' Per-minute pricing not shown on page; human tier is quote-based. Free trial not confirmed this session.

tools.name: aTrain
tools.description: Offline transcription of speech recordings with speaker detection (faster-whisper, 57 languages); exports transcripts with clickable timestamps directly importable into ATLAS.ti and MAXQDA. Installs from the Microsoft Store; no data ever sent to the internet.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Offline transcription that hands off straight into CAQDAS software with linked timestamps — audio playback from inside the coding environment Adoption: Peer-reviewed methods paper (Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance); listed in Temple University libguide and on McMaster University research-resources pages Overlaps with noScribe on the local-transcription task; differentiators are CAQDAS timestamp import and easy Windows Store install. Mac support less prominent.

tools.name: Evidano
tools.description: Uploads interview transcripts, documents, audio/video and runs thematic analysis with supporting quotes, frequency and cross-segment analysis, plus a chatbot over the data. Also fields an AI avatar that conducts semi-structured voice interviews in 100+ languages. Free tier available.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-conducted voice interviews — an avatar interviewer collects qualitative data autonomously, then the same platform analyzes it; no other vetted tool covers AI-led data collection Adoption: Formal software review by Christina Silver's CAQDAS Networking Project (University of Surrey, 2024, as AILYZE); site claims use at University of Texas, Cornell, University of Zambia Renamed from AILYZE (ailyze.com now 308-redirects to evidano.com). Claims GDPR/SOC2/HECVAT compliance; avatar interviews and transcription are paid add-ons. Company leadership not stated on site.

tools.name: MAXQDA AI Assist
tools.description: AI add-on inside the MAXQDA CAQDAS: suggests codes and subcodes for text passages with explanatory comments, summarizes documents and coded segments, and answers questions about coded data with responses linked to text sections. Claims zero data retention and EU-based processing.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI code suggestions embedded in the standard institutional coding workflow — keeps the audit trail and codebook of classic CAQDAS while accelerating first-pass coding Adoption: MAXQDA appears across university QDA libguides; multiple 2026 CAQDAS comparison articles cover AI Assist specifically Requires a MAXQDA license (~$440/yr individual; commonly site-licensed); AI Assist itself has free and premium tiers. ATLAS.ti and NVivo offer comparable AI - MAXQDA chosen as exemplar.

tools.name: noScribe
tools.description: Transcribes interview audio fully offline on the researcher's own computer using Whisper plus pyannote speaker diarization; marks pauses, overlaps and filler words per qualitative-research conventions; includes an audio-aligned correction editor. ~60 languages; Windows/macOS/Linux.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: GDPR-safe transcription of sensitive interview data — nothing leaves the machine, with transcript conventions (pauses, overlap, disfluencies) built for qualitative social research Adoption: Recommended in Temple University and University of Notre Dame qualitative-research libguides; developed by a sociologist for qualitative research 1h audio takes 1-3h CPU processing (faster with NVIDIA GPU). Donations-funded open source.

tools.name: QualCoder
tools.description: Free open-source CAQDAS (text, PDF, image, audio, video coding) with AI-assisted coding and AI chat over data. Uniquely, the underlying prompts are visible and editable; backends include OpenAI GPT-4 or Blablador, the Helmholtz Society's free no-data-stored academic LLM service.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Zero-cost, transparent AI-assisted qualitative coding — inspectable prompts plus a free EU academic LLM backend (Blablador) that stores no data; supports REFI-QDA exchange with commercial CAQDAS Adoption: Libguides at George Washington, University of Arizona, Temple, and University of Illinois; v4.0 released 2026 (actively maintained on GitHub) Desktop app, rougher UI than commercial CAQDAS; Blablador output quality below GPT-4 per its own docs. GitHub: https://github.com/ccbogel/QualCoder

tools.name: ASReview
tools.description: Runs active-learning screening locally: the model learns from your include/exclude decisions and reorders remaining records, with simulation mode to benchmark savings on your own dataset. Fully open source; data never leaves your machine.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: transparent, simulatable machine-learning screening you can audit and run offline — the only open-source option with a validation/simulation framework Adoption: Europe PMC: 313 Methods-section mentions; site reports 638k+ installations; v2.0 released, actively maintained on GitHub Single-reviewer paradigm by default (Crowdscreen adds collaboration); local install required, which is a feature for GDPR but a hurdle for novices.

tools.name: Covidence
tools.description: Manages the full PRISMA pipeline in one workspace: import, dedupe, dual screening, full-text review, data extraction, and quality assessment, with team roles and export to analysis. De-facto standard licensed by many university libraries.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Adoption: Europe PMC: 22,854 Methods-section mentions — the most-cited SR platform; institutional licenses common; Cochrane partnership referenced on site No free tier beyond a 500-record trial; personal plan $339/year per review. Check whether the university already licenses it before recommending purchase.

tools.name: DistillerSR
tools.description: Runs audit-trailed literature reviews at regulatory grade: AI reranking of references, automatic study classifiers, generative extraction linked back to source text, and error-checking of human screening decisions, all with traceable human-in-the-loop validation.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: regulatory-grade, fully audit-trailed AI extraction and screening quality control (pharma/medical-device evidence requirements) Adoption: Europe PMC: 1,374 Methods-section mentions; listed in King's College London libguide; site claims 80% of top pharma/device companies Contact-sales pricing (academic tier exists, figures unpublished); heavier than most student projects need — overlaps Covidence for basic workflows.

tools.name: Laser AI
tools.description: Extracts data from study PDFs by suggesting text passages and table values for reviewer confirmation, deduplicates references, and standardizes screening with reusable guides and vocabularies; built for living evidence synthesis feeding guideline pipelines.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-suggested extraction designed for the living-review-to-guideline pipeline (GRADE ecosystem via Evidence Prime) Adoption: Site lists McMaster University and IQWiG (German HTA agency) among clients; no independent Methods-mention count obtainable (name too ambiguous to query) Demo/contact-only access, plans from $3,000 — hence candidate. Extraction time-saving claims (53%) are vendor figures; HQ location not confirmed from fetched pages.

tools.name: Nested Knowledge
tools.description: Combines screening (Robot Screener), smart tagging, meta-analytical extraction, and PRISMA reporting with living-review updates: searches re-run automatically and interactive evidence maps and synthesis visualizations stay current and shareable.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: living systematic reviews with auto-updating searches plus publishable interactive synthesis visualizations Adoption: Europe PMC: 204 Methods-section mentions; free tier and ~$20/user/month academic pricing confirmed on provider's blog Main site is JS-only (details verified via about.nested-knowledge.com docs). Free tier limits collaboration; Smart features' validation studies linked but not assessed here.

tools.name: Rayyan
tools.description: Screen titles/abstracts in blinded reviewer pairs with AI relevance ranking, resolve up to 200k duplicates, run risk-of-bias assessment, and auto-generate PRISMA flow diagrams; free tier covers core screening.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Adoption: Europe PMC: 16,910 articles mention Rayyan in Methods sections; listed in King's College London systematic-review libguide GDPR/ISO 27001 claimed on site. New ResearchPilot AI features not independently evaluated; free-tier limits vs paid not itemized.

tools.name: eScriptorium
tools.provider: École Pratique des Hautes Études (EPHE) + Inria ALMAnaCH (France)
tools.description: Open-source web platform for segmenting and transcribing manuscripts and archival documents using the kraken HTR engine; researchers train or fine-tune their own recognition models and export ALTO/PAGE XML; self-hostable, IIIF-compatible.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Fully open-source, self-hosted HTR with owned models and data — no per-page credits, works for right-to-left and non-Latin scripts via kraken Adoption: UT Austin library blog feature (texlibris.lib.utexas.edu); step-by-step training guide maintained by Mannheim University Library; used in published models papers (Journal of Open Humanities Data) MIT license. Requires self-hosting or access to an institutional instance — more setup friction than Transkribus. Developed in France (EU).

tools.name: Handwriting OCR
tools.description: Uploads pages of contemporary handwriting — lab notebooks, field observation sheets, questionnaires, cursive letters — and returns searchable editable text; handles mixed hands, faded ink, and converts embedded equations to LaTeX.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Digitizing modern research handwriting (lab notebooks, field notes) with an explicit no-training-on-your-data policy — a privacy fit for unpublished data Adoption: Dedicated laboratory-notebook use-case page; no libguide or paper citation found this session Free trial credits; pay-as-you-go €15/100 pages. UK company, explicit no-model-training privacy claim; GDPR status inferred, not verified this session.

tools.name: Marker
tools.description: Open-source pipeline converting PDF, DOCX, PPTX, EPUB, and images to Markdown, JSON, or HTML with equations, tables, and reading order preserved — for building searchable or LLM-ready corpora from paper collections; runs locally.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Local, batch, no-cloud conversion of entire paper libraries to structured Markdown — data never leaves the machine Adoption: 38.8k GitHub stars, active commits; consistently top-ranked in 2026 open-source PDF-parser comparisons (vs MinerU, Docling) Code Apache 2.0; model weights non-commercial above $5M revenue. Hosted Datalab API exists for those who don't want to self-run. Needs Python + GPU for speed.

tools.name: Mathpix
tools.description: Screenshot-to-LaTeX OCR: converts images of equations, handwriting, chemistry structures, tables, and full PDFs into LaTeX, Markdown, DOCX, or CSV via the Snip desktop tool and editor. One keyboard shortcut turns any on-screen formula into paste-ready code.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: STEM-specific OCR — equations, handwritten math, and chemical structures to compilable LaTeX; sole representative of the 'get this formula out of a PDF' task Adoption: Referenced as the OCR component in a 2026 arXiv paper (mathematical forum platform, arXiv 2606.12976); long-standing researcher testimonials on site Snip Pro from $4.99/mo; free tier exists but per-month snip limits not confirmed this session. API is pay-as-you-go. No libguide sighting confirmed.

tools.name: Transcription Pearl
tools.provider: Wilfrid Laurier University (Humphries & Leddy, Dept. of History)
tools.description: Free desktop app that batch-transcribes archival page images through OpenAI, Gemini, or Claude APIs, showing each transcription beside its source image for correction and export — LLM-based mass transcription for historians.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Peer-review-backed LLM transcription workflow: the accompanying study found LLMs beat specialized HTR (Transkribus) on 18th/19th-c. English documents — the easter egg of this area Adoption: Companion paper published in Historical Methods (2025, DOI 10.1080/01615440.2025.2500309) and arXiv:2411.03340; GitHub repo public Beta; last commit Nov 2024 — maintenance uncertain. Requires own API keys and Python. CC BY-NC 4.0. Candidate until freshness confirmed.

tools.name: Transkribus
tools.description: Uploads scans of handwritten or printed historical documents and gets searchable transcriptions; trains custom recognition models for a specific hand, script, or language; recognizes tables and form fields.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Training a custom HTR model on one archive's specific handwriting, then batch-transcribing the collection — the standard platform for this in digital humanities Adoption: Dedicated LibGuide at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (unicatt.libguides.com/OCR-HTR/transkribus); ubiquitous in DH projects; used as the HTR baseline in the Humphries et al. 2024 arXiv paper Credit system: free 50 credits/month (~50 pages); Scholar €99/year. EU cooperative, states GDPR compliance. Strong EU/students story.

tools.name: LitSuggest
tools.description: Train a personal machine-learning classifier by marking PubMed articles relevant or irrelevant; the system then scores new PubMed papers, sends an automated weekly digest per project, and supports shared collaborative curation.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Building your own trainable literature-triage model — a personal classifier for systematic monitoring/curation, not just a keyword alert; free from NIH Adoption: Published system (Allot et al., Nucleic Acids Research 2021, W352–W358); still cited in recent curation workflows; no discontinuation notices found PubMed-only. Page is a single-page app, so features verified from the NAR paper and searches rather than the live UI; interface is dated.

tools.name: Paper Digest
tools.description: Daily email digest of new papers from arXiv, PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv and ClinicalTrials.gov, filtered by user-set areas, keywords and authors, with a machine-generated one-sentence summary per paper and impact-based ranking.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: One digest covering journals, preprints AND clinical-trial registrations, each item compressed to a single machine-written highlight sentence Adoption: Listed in the Breda University of Applied Sciences (BUas) libguide A–Z of AI tools; operating since 2018 Free tier covers arXiv/bioRxiv/medRxiv digests; paid from $6.66/month (annual). Small company; GDPR posture unverified (privacy policy PDF exists).

tools.name: R Discovery
tools.description: Personalized reading feed over 250M+ papers: set research interests, get daily article recommendations and new-paper alerts, listen to audio versions, translate papers into 30+ languages, and chat with PDFs on mobile or web.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Mobile-first commute-friendly literature feed — audio papers and translated summaries make it the 'podcast your feed' option Adoption: Listed in Bond University and University of Johannesburg libguides; 2.5M+ Android downloads, app updated May 2026 Prime tier ~$12/month unlocks audio/translation/unlimited use; free tier is real but upsell is persistent.

tools.name: Scholar Inbox
tools.provider: University of Tübingen (Autonomous Vision Group / Tübingen AI Center)
tools.description: Daily or weekly digest of new arXiv, bioRxiv, chemRxiv and medRxiv papers ranked by a recommender trained on the user's own ratings; includes semantic search, figure-preview skimming, collections, and a conference poster-session planner.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: An open academic-built personal recommender you train by voting on papers, spanning preprint servers plus ML/CV/NLP conference proceedings — with a conference planner nothing else offers Adoption: ACL 2025 system-demo paper (arXiv:2504.08385) reporting 23,000 registered and 8,000 monthly-active researchers; featured by Tübingen AI Center, which states developers plan to keep it free Corpus is ML/CS-centric though bio/med preprints are indexed; site is a JS app, details verified from the paper and Tübingen AI Center page.

tools.name: Stork
tools.description: Enter keywords and authors once; receive daily or weekly email alerts of matching new papers and preprints from PubMed and other sources, plus NIH grant-award alerts, with optional in-email translation of titles and abstracts.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Tracks NIH grant awards alongside papers — monitoring who just got funded in your field, not only who just published Adoption: Recommended in ResearchGate community threads on best literature-alert services; iOS app live; site active 2016–2026 Company identity not stated on site — a transparency caveat for students. Exact Pro/membership prices not captured. Bundled AI-writing tools not vetted here.

tools.name: ChatSlide
tools.description: Upload a paper or paste an abstract; generates a single-page academic poster (A0 or 36x48 in) with sectioned layout, charts rendered from your data, and PubMed/Scholar citation lookup. Exports print-locked PDF or editable pptx.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: No-code hosted paper-to-poster with print-size and editable-pptx export (the accessible counterpart to Paper2Poster) Adoption: Self-reported use at 750+ universities — unverified externally Free tier is 100 signup credits; paid from $99/yr. States GDPR compliance and has a privacy policy. Small SF startup; adoption claims are its own.

tools.name: Paper2Poster
tools.description: Multi-agent pipeline that converts a paper PDF into an editable PowerPoint conference poster: parses the paper into assets, plans a panel layout, renders and self-corrects with VLM feedback. Runs locally or via API models; Docker supported.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Fully automated paper-PDF-to-editable-pptx poster generation, open source and locally runnable Adoption: Accepted to NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks track; 3.9k GitHub stars; independent blog coverage (BrightCoding, Dec 2025) MIT license; needs an OpenAI API key or local vLLM models plus LibreOffice/poppler — technical setup, not point-and-click.

tools.name: Paper2Video
tools.description: Generates a complete conference presentation video from a paper: slides, synchronized subtitles, synthesized narration, cursor movements, and optional talking-head presenter from a reference photo and 10-second voice sample.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Automatic pre-recorded conference-talk video generation from a paper — relevant for virtual conferences requiring submitted videos Adoption: NeurIPS 2025 SEA workshop acceptance; 2.4k GitHub stars MIT license but demanding: LaTeX sources as input, Gemini/OpenAI keys, ~48GB-VRAM GPU for talking head (lighter slides-only mode exists). Research-grade, not turnkey.

tools.name: PowerPoint Speaker Coach
tools.description: Rehearse a talk against your actual slide deck inside PowerPoint (web, Windows, Mac, mobile); flags pacing, pitch, filler words, monotone delivery, and reading text off slides, then produces a rehearsal report with statistics.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Delivery coaching bound to the actual conference deck, inside software every university already licenses — zero new accounts Adoption: Current Microsoft support documentation (fetched); UNC ITS 'Become a better public speaker' recommendation page seen in search results English-only interface requirement for the coach; needs microphone and internet. Free preview per Microsoft docs, but preview terms can change.

tools.name: VirtualSpeech
tools.description: Rehearse a talk in simulated rooms (conference room, lecture hall, press conference — 13 environments) via browser or VR headset; AI scores body language, eye contact, pace, and filler words, and asks questions generated from your presentation content.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Simulated-audience rehearsal in a virtual conference/lecture environment, including VR Adoption: G2 review page exists (seen in search); no academic library-guide adoption found $45/mo or $399/yr, no free trial found on pricing page; corporate-training oriented. UK company; EU-friendliness not confirmed.

tools.name: Yoodli
tools.description: Records a practice talk via webcam or uploaded video and scores filler words, pacing, eye contact, clarity, and structure, benchmarking each rehearsal against the last; AI follow-up questions simulate audience Q&A after a conference talk.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Quantified delivery feedback across repeated rehearsals of the same conference talk, plus simulated Q&A Adoption: Recommended on University of Hawai'i–West O'ahu official Distance Learning student-resources page (fetched); UW career-center resource page seen in search results Free tier is only 5 lifetime sessions; Pro $8/mo billed annually. Paid Advanced tier needed to exclude data from AI training.

tools.name: OpenAI Prism
tools.description: Free AI-native LaTeX workspace on GPT-5.2: whole-document writing and proofreading assistance, reference management, image-to-LaTeX for photographed equations and whiteboard sketches, agentic literature search with citation suggestions, and real-time collaboration with unlimited collaborators.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: A full AI-first LaTeX editor free with any ChatGPT account — the whole-document AI context (not per-sentence) plus built-in arXiv literature agent Adoption: HKUST Library news page recommending it to academic writers (fetched); Engadget and The Decoder launch coverage seen in search; app live at prism.openai.com (fetched, sign-in shell) Built on acquired Crixet platform. Cloud-only; HKUST cautions on uploading unpublished/sensitive work and possible future paywalling of advanced features. openai.com/prism blocks bot fetching (403).

tools.name: Overleaf AI Assist
tools.description: AI built into the standard collaborative LaTeX editor: explains and fixes LaTeX compile errors, generates tables and equations from images or prompts (TeXGPT), and gives Writefull-powered language feedback trained on published papers. Free daily allowances on all plans.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: LaTeX error diagnosis and repair inside the editor 20M+ researchers already write in — no copy-pasting code into a chatbot Adoption: Official overleaf.com/about/ai-features page (fetched); docs.overleaf.com AI-features pages; Overleaf blog 'Overleaf AI now a part of Overleaf plans' (July 2026); Overleaf itself appears across university libguides (e.g. Bristol) Since July 2026 included in all plans with daily caps (quota resets ~72h); paid plans raise allowances. Error assist uses OpenAI as third party.

tools.name: Papers AI
tools.provider: Digital Science (built by the Overleaf team)
tools.description: Offline-first AI research workspace: write in LaTeX, Typst, Markdown or Word alongside Jupyter notebooks and CSVs, with a context-aware assistant that reads drafts, data and references together. Compiles locally in-browser; can run entirely on local models via Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-assisted scholarly writing that never sends data to the cloud (local models, local compile) — the GDPR/sensitive-data option; also the only AI-assisted Typst workflow found Adoption: Digital Science press release, launch 4 Aug 2026 (fetched); product page live with free tier (fetched); too new for libguides Two weeks old at review time — no independent adoption evidence yet. Distinct from ReadCube Papers despite the name. Paid-tier pricing not published on fetched pages.

tools.name: Trinka
tools.description: Upload a .tex file and get it proofread with LaTeX commands untouched: returns a corrected LaTeX file plus a Word file with tracked changes, a language-quality score, and revision breakdown. Style-guide aware (APA, AMA, IEEE).
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Batch proofreading of a whole .tex manuscript outside any editor, with tracked-changes Word output co-authors can review — bridges LaTeX and Word-based collaborators Adoption: Official Trinka feature and news pages (fetched); G2 review presence seen in search; no libguide sighting confirmed Credit-based: 1 credit per 5,000 words, 4 free credits/month on Basic. Parent Enago also behind catalog's 'Enago AI Disclosure' — different product. Broader Trinka overlaps Paperpal; propose only the LaTeX proofreader angle.

tools.name: Writefull
tools.description: Language feedback for scientific text from models trained on millions of published journal articles, delivered inside Overleaf (edits in LaTeX source), Word, or a standalone Revise uploader. Adds paraphrasing, abstract/title generation, and TeXGPT table/equation code generation.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Sentence-level feedback calibrated to published-paper conventions rather than general English; corrections applied directly within LaTeX source code Adoption: Multiple university libguides fetched via search: Montclair State, CSIR (South Africa), Nazarbayev University; integrated natively into Overleaf Premium ~$150/yr (June 2026 listing). Writefull Cite (flags sentences needing a citation) is institution-license only. States texts are not stored or used for training.

tools.name: Expected Parrot
tools.description: Open-source Python DSL for building surveys and experiments, running them on panels of LLM-simulated respondents across many models, then re-fielding the identical instrument to real humans ('Humanize') and analyzing both in one results object.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Programmatic pretesting of survey instruments and factorial experiments on simulated respondents before spending real participants, with a built-in AI-to-human validation bridge Adoption: MIT-licensed on GitHub/PyPI; co-founded by economist John Horton (citation: Horton & Horton 2024 whitepaper); docs carry a Papers & Citations page; own docs warn simulated responses reflect training data, not real populations Free Coop credits at signup, extra free credits for researchers on request, or bypass credits entirely with your own API keys. YC F25 company.

tools.name: NC3Rs Experimental Design Assistant
tools.description: Free web tool where researchers diagram an in vivo experiment and receive automated bespoke critique: statistical-method recommendations, randomization and blinding support, sample-size calculation, and a shareable design report for funders and ethical review.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Machine-critiqued animal-experiment design producing reports that Wellcome encourages and NIH can request with grant applications Adoption: 16,000+ registered users since 2015; NC3Rs pages document Wellcome and NIH uptake of EDA reports in funding applications Automated critique is rule-based expert-system style, not generative LLM; include as AI-adjacent design assistant. Uniquely strong academic legitimacy for this area.

tools.name: Protocol Builder
tools.description: Drafts clinical research protocols and informed-consent forms section-by-section from institutional templates; the built-in AI assistant completes sections, generates consent drafts from protocol text, and rewrites consent language at an 8th-grade reading level.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: structured IRB protocol and consent-form authoring with compliance templates Adoption: Sold to IRBs and GME programs; BRANY is an established IRB/compliance services organization; site current (screenshots dated March 2026) Demo-only, no public pricing — hence candidate. US clinical-research centric; EU ethics-committee fit unverified.

tools.name: Qualtrics AI
tools.description: Survey platform most universities already license: ExpertReview audits draft questionnaires for methodology errors, PII risk, and accessibility before launch; Synthetic Panels answer a survey with a first-party AI model trained on real survey responses.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI methodology review and synthetic piloting inside the survey platform academics already field studies from Adoption: Ubiquitous institutional licensing; Duke CTSI runs Qualtrics survey-design training (seen in search); support docs confirm Synthetic Panels is a shipped, documented feature Synthetic Panels gated to newer pricing plans plus purchased credits, US general population, English only; academic licenses may lack it. ExpertReview is broadly available. Verify campus entitlements.

tools.name: Synthetic Users
tools.description: Runs no-code simulated qualitative studies: multi-agent AI participants with persistent persona profiles answer interviews, concept tests, and usability-style questions in minutes, at $2-60 per interview instead of recruiting humans.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Turnkey simulated qualitative interviews for early problem discovery and concept testing without recruitment Adoption: Publishes a /science validation section claiming 85-92% synthetic-organic parity; widely debated: NN/g article 'Synthetic Users: If, When, and How' explicitly warns against substituting for real users Controversial by design: NN/g documents sycophancy and uniformly positive feedback; defensible for hypothesis generation and piloting, not for validation claims. Free demo, no ongoing free tier confirmed.

tools.name: Audemic Scholar
tools.description: Reads uploaded or reference-manager-imported papers aloud with synchronized text highlighting; reorder sections, capture highlights and notes. Dyslexia-friendly fonts, background color options, and adjustable pacing support researchers with dyslexia, ADHD, or visual impairment.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Accessibility-adapted consumption of research papers (dyslexia, ADHD, visual impairment) Adoption: Site claims 40,000+ users from institutions; Berkeley SkyDeck-backed; iOS/Android app-store listings 7-day free trial then $20/mo or ~$109/yr. Listed awards/updates cluster in 2023; 2026 activity not directly confirmed.

tools.name: Cassyni
tools.description: Runs and records research seminars, then AI-enhances them: transcripts, slide extraction, semantic chapters, resolved references to cited papers, and a DOI per talk — turning seminars into citable, searchable scholarly objects researchers can browse.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: publishing and discovering research talks as DOI-citable parts of the scholarly record Adoption: Imperial College London Graduate School runs a Cassyni seminar program for PhD students; partnerships with Frontiers, Springer Nature, Elsevier, Royal Society (2023-2025 press) Attending/browsing seminars free; hosting a series is institutional/publisher-paid. Landing page is minimal; capabilities verified via press and Imperial pages.

tools.name: ElevenReader
tools.description: Free reader app from ElevenLabs that voices PDFs, preprints, and web articles with realistic neural voices, reading abbreviations naturally ('e.g.' as 'for example'). 10 free hours monthly; Ultra ($99/yr) adds smart imports that strip headers and footers.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Adoption: Genomics researcher Stephen Turner's 'Paired Ends' Substack (Apr 2025) documents using it to listen to preprints and papers General-purpose reader, not academia-specific; no citation skipping. GenFM podcast feature not confirmed on current site.

tools.name: Kudos
tools.description: Researcher creates a free showcase page explaining a publication in plain language; Kudos's AI service drafts the summary and a paid campaign promotes it via email, social media, and themed showcases, with tracked views, Altmetric scores, and citations.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Publishing and promoting plain-language summaries of published papers with impact tracking Adoption: Kudos blog documents AI Summaries rollout with publishers and author-verdict testing; university partnership coverage (Sheffield Hallam) seen in search results Free account is self-write; AI-drafted summary confirmed in the $499 researcher campaign and publisher services. Self-serve AI drafting on free tier unconfirmed.

tools.name: Listening
tools.description: Converts paper PDFs into natural-sounding audio that automatically skips citations, references, and footnotes; listen by section (abstract, results) at up to 4x speed. Mobile apps and Chrome extension for consuming a reading backlog while commuting.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Full-text listening to academic PDFs with citation/footnote skipping and section-level navigation Adoption: Site claims 50,000+ users; iOS/Android app-store presence; frequently compared in academic TTS roundups; no libguide sighting $12.99/mo or $39/yr promo; no free tier on pricing page (third-party listing mentions 1-week trial). GDPR posture unverified.

tools.name: PaperTok
tools.provider: University of Washington Prosocial Computing Group
tools.description: Generates roughly 45-second short-form explainer videos from an uploaded paper PDF using Gemini; the researcher iteratively edits the script and visuals before rendering, for TikTok/Reels-style science communication. Open-source codebase; presented at CHI 2026.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Paper to short-form social video for public science communication Adoption: CHI 2026 paper (Barcelona, April 2026); TechXplore coverage June 2026 Academic prototype, live site with generate button; requires user's paid Google Gemini subscription. Privacy policy and durability unverified.

tools.name: Wondercraft
tools.description: Turns an uploaded paper or URL into a conversational podcast episode; edit the script word-by-word, choose or clone voices, add team review flows, then export WAV or publish toward Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Free tier includes starter credits.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Producing a publishable, edited outreach podcast episode from a paper (vs. NotebookLM's non-editable private overviews) General podcast studio with a dedicated research-paper workflow; free 150 credits, Creator $25/mo. Academic adoption unverified.

tools.name: Argos
tools.description: Screens a reference list for retracted and high-risk articles before submission and sends alerts when papers in your citation network are retracted; computes daily risk scores from author histories and retraction cascades across 50M+ articles.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: retraction-risk screening of references plus proactive retraction-cascade alerts Adoption: Oncotarget lists Argos on its scientific-integrity process page; Duke Medical Center Library blog covers it among retraction-identification tools Free account 'for the entire scientific community'; institutional tier priced on request. Public benefit corporation. 2025 statistics on site.

tools.name: Imagetwin
tools.description: Scans figures (western blots, microscopy, photos) for duplications, manipulations, and AI-generated images; matches against a 150M+ published-figure database to catch cross-paper reuse. Pay-per-scan from EUR 29 makes lab-level pre-submission screening feasible.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Cross-paper figure matching against 150M+ published figures, purchasable as a EUR 29 one-off scan — no publisher subscription needed (Proofig's catalog entry is manuscript-level screening) Adoption: Mass General Brigham Research Computing licenses it for its researchers (rc.partners.org page, fetched), including honest guidance on limitations MGB flags a notable false-negative rate; scatterplots/FACS not covered. Differentiation vs Proofig taken from vendor pages, not independently benchmarked.

tools.name: Pangram
tools.description: Classifies text as human- or AI-written with per-document and per-sentence results via web dashboard and API; 20 free checks daily. Reports a 1-in-10,000 false-positive rate, with an independent University of Chicago evaluation.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-text detection with the only independently evaluated sub-0.5% false-positive rate — usable for editorial screening where accusation stakes are high Adoption: arXiv technical report 2402.14873; a 2025 University of Chicago evaluation (seen via search + vendor third-party-evals page) found it the only detector meeting an FPR<=0.005 policy cap All AI-text detection is probabilistic — never sole evidence against an author. Headline accuracy figures are vendor-reported; one independent academic eval, which I saw summarized, not in full.

tools.name: Problematic Paper Screener
tools.provider: Guillaume Cabanac, IRIT / Universite de Toulouse (with Labbe & Magazinov)
tools.description: Browsable dashboard screening 130M+ papers with detectors for tortured phrases, SCIgen/Mathgen text, citejacking, retracted references, and problematic cell lines. Check a DOI before citing it, or trawl your field for flagged papers.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: The only public tool for checking whether a specific published paper is flagged for tortured phrases, mass-produced text, or reliance on retracted work — post-publication integrity screening for readers, not publishers Adoption: Peer-reviewed description (arXiv 2210.04895); coverage in The Conversation, Science, TechXplore; coverage credits it with contributing to 1000+ retractions Landing URL redirects to an Oracle APEX app (dbrech.irit.fr/pls/apex/f?p=9999) — data verified fresh, last update 2026-08-13. Academic side project, not a company.

tools.name: RefCheckAI
tools.provider: Sydney Informatics Hub, University of Sydney
tools.description: Checks whether each citation statement is actually supported by the cited source, classifying claims as supported, partially supported, not supported, or uncertain, with evidence snippets. Fine-tuned open Llama 3.1 model; free for non-commercial use.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Semantic citation verification — whether the cited paper supports the claim, not merely whether the reference exists (scite shows citation context but does not classify your own manuscript's claims) Adoption: University-built (Sydney Informatics Hub, NCI/NVIDIA-supported CodeFest); model weights and training data published for download Early access — web app via registration/email only. Classification accuracy not independently benchmarked. CC BY-NC 4.0.

tools.name: statcheck
tools.description: Upload a PDF, DOCX, or HTML manuscript; it recomputes every APA-style statistical result (t, F, r, chi-square, Z, Q) and flags p-values inconsistent with the reported test statistic and degrees of freedom.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: recomputation-based consistency check of reported statistics — a spellchecker for stats Adoption: Used in the review workflow of Psychological Science and Journal of Experimental Social Psychology; R package on CRAN; own Wikipedia entry Rule-based automation, not an LLM — flag if catalog is strictly 'AI'. Requires APA-formatted stats; misses tables. v1.5.0 (2024). Files not stored.

tools.name: BenchSci
tools.description: Finds validated antibodies and reagents by AI-decoding figures and usage evidence from 20M+ publications and 14M commercial products; filter by application, species reactivity, and validation status before ordering. Free for verified academic and nonprofit researchers.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Antibody/reagent selection grounded in AI-decoded published figures — directly attacks the antibody reproducibility crisis; nothing else in the catalog covers reagent choice Adoption: re3data.org registry entry; the Node (Company of Biologists) writeup; academic sign-up link live on benchsci.com; Stanford and Harvard listed as users Company now leads with enterprise agentic platform EMET; academic antibody-search sign-up still linked but current UI/scope not testable without institutional login. Requires affiliation verification.

tools.name: Genemod
tools.description: ELN/LIMS/inventory platform with an embedded AI agent that drafts experiment write-ups, registers samples, and updates inventory records from a single instruction, every action audit-trailed; equipment and order management for academic departments.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Conversational agent acting over lab inventory and sample records (the inventory/ordering AI slot), or null if judged too close to generic ELN AI Adoption: Capterra and FitGap listings; own academic-labs pricing packages Weakest vetting: genemod.net pages repeatedly failed direct fetch (oversized pages); AI-agent and pricing claims come from genemod.net snippets via search. ~$199/month, 14-day trial, annual contract; no confirmed permanent free tier.

tools.name: OpentronsAI
tools.description: Generates executable, inspectable Python protocols for Opentrons liquid-handling robots from a natural-language description of the experiment, with in-chat simulation, verification, and deck-map visualization. Sign-up works even without owning a robot.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Natural language to lab-robot protocol code — the only bench-automation entry point a student can try without hardware Adoption: Coverage in SelectScience, The Robot Report, SynBioBeta; Opentrons robots are common in academic labs; RAG architecture over verified protocol library Page does not explicitly say free forever — 'Sign up to try' with no pricing shown. Output only useful for labs with (or considering) Opentrons hardware.

tools.name: protocols.io AI
tools.description: Drafts structured protocols from prompts or Word/PDF uploads, suggests error-reduction and troubleshooting fixes, translates private protocols across 36 languages, and summarizes reviewer feedback — inside the standard platform for publishing versioned, citable methods.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-assisted authoring and troubleshooting of citable, versioned wet-lab protocols in the community-standard protocol repository (23,000+ public protocols) Adoption: Springer Nature press release 2025-12-17; Nature Protocols partnership page; librarian licensing page confirms free accounts plus institutional plans Homepage blocks WebFetch (403); could not confirm which tier gets which AI features — press release notes some areas require subscription. AI launch was Dec 2025, so features are new.

tools.name: SciNote AI
tools.description: Electronic lab notebook whose AI converts PDF-based SOPs and protocols into structured, reusable ELN templates and auto-updates task/project progress from user activity; includes inventory management and compliance tools. Core ELN is open source; free plan for individuals.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI parsing of legacy PDF SOPs into structured, executable ELN templates Adoption: Open-source repo scinote-eln/scinote-web on GitHub; coverage in Scientific Computing World and Lab Manager; Ascenscia voice-assistant partnership EU HQ (+386 Slovenia) — good GDPR angle, but Trust Center details not verified. AI features likely premium-only; tier assignment unconfirmed.

tools.name: CAS SciFinder Prior Art
tools.description: Inside CAS SciFinder: paste 200+ characters of invention text (claims or abstract) and AI algorithm streams return similar patents and non-patent literature published before your priority date, drawing on CAS's human-curated chemistry collection including Markush structures.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Chemistry-aware prior-art search over curated substance/Markush indexing — inside a database most chemistry-active universities already license, so no new procurement Adoption: Temple and Rutgers library AI-features guides both list Prior Art Discovery as an AI feature of CAS SciFinder Requires an institutional SciFinder subscription; direct product-help page returned 403, feature confirmed via cas.org and two libguides. CAS Newton conversational AI is a separate, newer layer.

tools.name: Google Patents
tools.description: Free worldwide patent full-text search with ML features: machine-classified CPC code suggestions, 'Similar' documents ranked by a full-text model, one-click 'Find prior art' scoped to before the priority date, SMILES chemical-structure search, and Google Scholar non-patent literature integration.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Zero-cost first-look prior-art check with priority-date-aware 'Find prior art' across patents, Scholar and Books simultaneously Adoption: Standard entry in university patent libguides (Michigan State, Iowa State, Texas A&M, Pitt appeared in searches); Google Research blog documents the Prior Art Finder Help page (support.google.com/faqs/answer/7049475) confirms features; main page is a JS app so feature claims verified via help page and libguides.

tools.name: InventGenie
tools.description: Turns research papers, notes and technical input into structured invention-disclosure building blocks: draft patent claims, specification text and figure suggestions, formatted for tech-transfer review, with multi-inventor collaboration. Pay-per-draft ($180) or monthly seat pricing; attorney review still required before filing.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI drafting of the invention disclosure itself, aimed explicitly at university researchers and tech transfer — the only researcher-facing (not attorney-facing) drafting tool found Real but young company; no independent academic adoption found; no free tier. Confidentiality caution: check TTO policy before pasting unfiled invention details into third-party AI (UC Berkeley OTL advises exactly this).

tools.name: PatSnap
tools.description: AI innovation-intelligence platform: patent landscape maps, novelty and FTO search agents (Eureka), drafting agents, litigation and market data, biosequence and chemical structure search. Tech transfer offices use it to judge whether an invention's space is commercially active before funding proof-of-concept.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: TTO-grade commercial landscape triage — 'who is active in this space and is it heating up' — before deciding to file Adoption: Published customer case study: City, University of London technology transfer office uses it for landscape analysis of academic inventions (replaced manual Espacenet work) Enterprise pricing via demo; Eureka offers a free trial. Recommendable mainly where the university already licenses it; individuals cannot simply subscribe at list price.

tools.name: PQAI
tools.provider: Project PQAI (nonprofit initiative, AT&T / Georgia IP Alliance)
tools.description: Paste a plain-language invention description; deep-learning models trained on examiner citation data return ranked prior art from USPTO, EPO and open-access journals, plus concept extraction and CPC/IPC code suggestions. Open-source (MIT), free web search and API.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Free, open-source semantic prior-art search an academic can run before submitting an invention disclosure; API is explicitly pitched at university tech transfer offices Adoption: Unified Patents support article describes it; site has a 'For University Tech Transfer Offices' page; active GitHub org (pqaidevteam); 2025-2026 dated content Coverage is USPTO/EPO + DOAJ, not all jurisdictions; results are a first-pass screen, not a professional novelty search.

tools.name: The Lens
tools.provider: The Lens Limited (Australian non-profit, formerly Cambia)
tools.description: Links 155M+ patent records with 270M+ scholarly works: landscape dashboards, patent-to-paper citation mapping, PatSeq search for DNA/protein sequences inside patents, freedom-to-operate style filtering. Free personal accounts for academic researchers (exports up to 50,000 records); institutional toolkit for universities.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Seeing which patents cite your own papers, and finding biological sequences buried in patents (PatSeq) — the scholarly-patent bridge no general assistant or single-corpus tool covers Adoption: Listed on WIPO Inspire; peer-reviewed review article in PMC; explicit cost-free academic personal accounts and Lens Equitable Access Program Ownership moved to non-profit The Lens Limited June 2026. Strength is authoritative linked data, not generative AI — release notes show few AI features; commercial individual use is $1,000/yr.

tools.name: B!SON
tools.description: Paste a manuscript's title, abstract, and references; machine-learning similarity against DOAJ article and citation data ranks quality-assured open-access journals publishing similar work, with transparent per-journal reasoning and an open API.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: manuscript-driven open-access journal selection (no journal-selection tool in catalog) Adoption: SLUB Dresden library service page; DOAJ blog feature dated 2026-07-08 confirming monthly data updates; institutions can host custom instances Open source, German library-run, privacy-friendly — strong EU/GDPR fit. Landing page is a JS app; capability details verified via DOAJ/TIB pages.
